summary: The inbox project gave agents a place to leave you two kinds of item: a question to answer and a notice to read. An agent posts one with project inbox ask or project inbox tell, or with the ask and tell tools in Claude Code, and Projector's band, the panel above the Claude Code prompt, lists it until you answer, dismiss, or snooze it. That work shipped across releases 0.7.15 to 0.7.18, and three follow-ups are on main for the next release: #303 changes the band further, #305 lets an agent withdraw an item it posted, and #319 makes only a picked option answer a question.

This pull request closes the project. The plan said it would stay in-progress until the owner checked one acceptance row by hand: on Claude Code's main screen under tmux, ctrl+x tab and Enter on an item opens its drawer. The owner has now made that check, so the plan's status becomes completed and a new § 12 records the outcome. One band test is added for a § 10 row whose evidence was indirect. This head also merges main, where #319 appended § 13, "A reply leaves a question open", so § 12 sits before § 13 and refers to it.

Projector's rules for plans, in docs/projects/README.md, say a completed plan states whether it shipped, was abandoned, or was superseded, and the finish skill asks that every acceptance criterion have evidence or a stated reason it is not delivered. § 12 is where this plan meets both.

cards.title: Terms on this page
cards.html:
• Item: a question or a notice an agent posted to the inbox.
  • The band: Projector's panel above the Claude Code prompt, which lists pull requests and inbox items.
  • Drawer: the detail an item or pull request expands into when you open its line in the band.
  • Acceptance row: one line of a plan's acceptance table, an action and the result it must produce.
  • Reply: under § 13, anything you send under a quoted question that is not one of its options. It leaves the question open.

  • Earlier rounds settled the citation of the test #303 renamed and an earlier wrap fix.

groups.title: The plan records its outcome
groups.kicker: Status completed, and a new § 12 that accounts for every acceptance row
intro: The plan's frontmatter changes from in-progress to completed. Its priority stays now, as on the repository's other completed plans; Projector requires no priority once a plan is completed.

§ 9 and § 11.10 each ended by saying the project stays in-progress until the hand check. Both sentences now say it stayed in-progress until the check that § 12 records, so the history reads correctly beside the new status. § 6 and § 10 are untouched. The merge with main brings in § 13 from #319. This pull request's last commit reconciles § 12 with it: § 12.2 now says only an option answers a question, § 12.3 marks the § 10 row for a typed answer as superseded, and § 12.4 drops revising in place from the work left undone.

1. § 12.1 What shipped lists each release and the pull requests in it, and #303, which is on main after 0.7.18.
  2. § 12.2 How the result differs from § 2 collects the deviations that § 9, § 10, and § 11 record, such as answering under a quoted question in the prompt in place of a Type something field, and numbering each session's items from 1.
  3. § 12.3 Evidence maps each acceptance row of § 4, § 10, and § 11.8 to the test that pins it, or to the owner's hand check.
  4. § 12.4 What this project does not deliver lists the open questions in § 7 that stay out of the project, such as a session's id outside Claude Code.

groups.title: A test for the shared age column
groups.kicker: A pull request's age and an item's age end in one column
intro: Each line in the band ends with an age, such as 5m. § 10 says pull requests and inbox items share one right-aligned age column, as wide as the widest age in the band. The existing test drew only pull requests, so the items' part of that rule had no test.
The new test puts a pull request updated 5 minutes ago beside a question posted 12 minutes ago, and checks that both ages take the 3-column width of 12m.

files.note: One new test beside the band's other tool and item tests.

checks.text: The test fails when the items' ages are removed from ageWidth in hooks/register.tsx, while the other plugin tests pass, and passes with the code as it is. Checked by editing a scratch copy and running claude plugin test ..
